dedupe_keys.name: national highway planning network nhpn fhwa geospatial highway network

description: The National Highway Planning Network is a geospatial network database of line features representing just over 450,000 miles of US highways. It holds geospatially referenced information on the National Highway System, the Eisenhower Interstate System and the Strategic Highway Network (STRAHNET), among others. FHWA has used it to map the NHS, track which roads belong to it, serve as a base network for mapping and GIS, and model freight flows in the Freight Analysis Framework. Version 14.05 is built from road networks that states submitted with their Highway Performance Monitoring System data, and is offered as zip files in several formats with a metadata document describing the attributes. Coverage: US highways. Format and access: free downloads. Licence and cost: free; no licence is stated. Caveats: a planning-level network whose version date should be checked against newer HPMS releases. It supports network flow and hazard exposure studies of the US highway system. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework, HPMS and the National Transportation Atlas Database in the catalogue.
